correctness.rationale: For finite d>=3 and lengths n_i>=2, the stable equitable partition distinguishes distance ranks from the marked origin and from the unique opposite corner. The predecessor-deck reconstruction recovers each coordinate-value multiset by S_0=p a_0+a_1 and S_j=(p-1)a_j+a_{j+1} for j>=1, starting at a_0=d-p. Reversal gives the complementary multiset from the top; neighbor-card signed differences recover the paired coordinate values and complementary values, including the x_i=0 boundary by successors. This joint multiset determines exactly the orbit under equal-factor permutations; automorphisms preserve stable colors, hence equality. The proof covers every quantifier boundary and does not extrapolate finite tests. Independent programs from saved files checked direct refinement, weighted quotient, actual automorphism partitions and exact reconstruction identities; all passed.

value.rationale: One-root orbit recovery in all higher-dimensional rectangular grid graphs is a natural all-orders counting-logic classification, not a routine parameter substitution from d=2 or from a poset with full comparability relation. The joint two-corner coordinate reconstruction explains a structural phenomenon not visible from rank or separate coordinate marginals and yields exact uniform orbit-count and class-size formulas with unbounded dimension and mixed factor lengths. The result is self-contained and does not require a sharp stabilization-depth or global identification theorem.
